title: Why Your Savings Shrink Even When the Balance Doesn't
description:
Your savings balance can stay the same while its buying power quietly falls. Using a stickman on a down escalator, this video explains inflation, the Consumer Price Index, and the difference between nominal and real interest rates, with U.S. data as of September 2026 (3.7% annual CPI inflation vs. a 0.38% national average savings rate).

In this video:
- Hook: standing still on a down escalator
- The problem: what $100 from 2020 and 2016 buys today
- Why it happens: inflation, CPI, and core inflation
- How it works: relative motion and the real interest rate (0.38% - 3.7% = about -3.2%)
- The faster walker: high-yield savings vs. inflation
- Who controls the escalator: the Federal Reserve and its 2% target
- What it means for you: raises, rates, and emergency funds
- Rule of 72: how fast prices double
- Conclusion
